title_clean: Pre-Open Market Explained - Trading from 9AM to 9:07AM
summary: Mechanics of the NSE pre-open session: order entry 9:00-9:07 with modification allowed, random freeze possible 9:07-9:08, then equilibrium-price auction at 9:15. Full worked example of demand/supply aggregation and maximum-tradeable-quantity logic that sets the opening price.
lessons: Pre-open is an order-collection auction: buy/sell orders accumulate 9:00-9:07; the exchange can freeze randomly 9:07-9:08, so finish changes before 9:07.
Opening price = the price where maximum quantity can trade after stacking cumulative demand (down) and supply (up).
Match priority at auction: limit-limit first, then residual limit vs market, then market-market.

title_clean: How Traders Fail - Recovery Mindset and Gambler's Fallacy
summary: Two failure patterns: (1) the 'recover my loss' mindset - lost capital is sunk; a trader who learns to make 5 lakh/month will not quit after 'recovering', so trade fresh capital for decent returns; (2) gambler's fallacy - streaks don't change probabilities (Monte Carlo 1913: 26 reds; SBI falling 5 days says nothing about day 6). Nick Leeson's short strangle doubled down on 'it can't fall more' and Kobe earthquake destroyed Barings.
lessons: There is no such thing as recovering a loss - the money lost is tuition; treat remaining capital as fresh and target decent returns on it.
Gambler's fallacy: past streaks don't change next-day probabilities - a 5-day fall can continue on day 6.
Overbought can stay overbought and oversold oversold until you go bankrupt - never average/double down because 'it has fallen too much'.
